trump-01.name: I · Le Bateleur
trump-01.Scene: A conjurer stands at a small three-legged table, his wide-brimmed red hat shading his face. He holds a wand or baton in his right hand and gestures over the objects spread before him. The figure is compact and confident, rendered in the flat woodcut style typical of 17th-century Parisian playing cards.

trump-02.name: II · La Papesse
trump-02.Scene: A winged crowned figure sits frontally, large dark wings spread behind them, reading or holding an open book. Unlike the standard seated Papesse of Marseille tradition, this figure has an angelic or supernatural quality — crown and wings together suggesting celestial authority rather than a church office.

trump-03.name: III · L'Impératrice
trump-03.Scene: A winged empress sits enthroned, holding an imperial sceptre topped with a cross in one hand and an eagle-emblazoned shield in the other. The wings and the heraldic eagle mark her as both earthly ruler and celestial power, a figure of imperium that blends military and divine authority.

trump-04.name: IIII · L'Empereur
trump-04.Scene: A bearded emperor stands in strict profile, holding an orb topped with a cross. Below him an eagle spreads its wings at the card's base, grounding the image in heraldic tradition. Unlike the frontally seated emperor of standard Marseille decks, this standing profile figure conveys active authority rather than static dominion.

trump-05.name: V · Le Pape
trump-05.Scene: An enthroned pope sits between two decorated pillars, raising a hand in blessing. Two smaller figures kneel before him in the lower portion of the card, their heads bowed in reverence. The composition follows the standard Marseille papal model with the Viéville's characteristic woodcut economy.

trump-06.name: VI · L'Amoureux
trump-06.Scene: Three young men stand together in close proximity, their faces turned slightly toward one another. Above them hovers a large radiant Cupid putto with wings spread, aiming downward. Unusually, there are no women in this image — the Viéville L'Amoureux depicts a homosocial trio under love's influence rather than the more common scene of a man choosing between two women.

trump-07.name: VII · La Justice
trump-07.Scene: A winged crowned woman holds an upright sword in her right hand and scales in her left, Justice personified. She is placed at position VII — before the Chariot — in the Viéville ordering, an arrangement that differs from many Marseille variants and reflects an older numbering tradition.

trump-08.name: VIII · Le Chariot
trump-08.Scene: A canopied baldachin structure shelters a crowned figure seated within it, while two smaller crowned figures stand or kneel below. The Viéville Le Chariot at position VIII is entirely architectural — no horses, no wheels, the throne itself serving as the vehicle of authority.

trump-09.name: VIIII · La Force
trump-09.Scene: A figure in a plumed hat grasps a lion from above, subduing it with both hands. The struggle is energetic — La Force at position IX in the Viéville uses the classical image of man dominating beast, but the plumed hat gives the figure a hunter's or soldier's aspect rather than the graceful lady of later tradition.

trump-10.name: X · La Roue de Fortune
trump-10.Scene: A large circular wheel mechanism fills the card, its spokes and rim clearly rendered as a spinning device. A crowned figure perches at the top, while other figures cling to the descending sides. Fortune is rendered as a literal turning wheel rather than an allegorical emblem, mechanical and inexorable.

trump-11.name: XI · L'Hermite
trump-11.Scene: A bearded man in a long robe gathers or opens a large cloak or mantle around himself, his body partly concealed in its folds. No lantern is visible — the Viéville Hermite at position XI expresses his solitude through his relationship with cloth rather than light, the gesture of wrapping suggesting concealment and revelation simultaneously.

trump-12.name: XII · Le Pendu
trump-12.Scene: A young figure stands upright between two tall decorated poles, feet planted firmly on the ground. In direct contrast to the inverted Hanged Man of other Marseille decks, there is no inversion here — the figure stands, not hangs. The two poles and the figure's position between them suggest suspension or liminal state without the dramatic reversal.

trump-13.name: XIII · La Mort
trump-13.Scene: An energetic skeleton moves across the field, wielding a large red scythe in a sweeping arc. From the ground beneath the blade, severed hands and limbs emerge. The skeleton's posture is dynamic, almost dancing, and the red scythe lends the image both violence and a vivid chromatic intensity unusual in cards of this period.

trump-14.name: XIIII · Tempérance
trump-14.Scene: A standing crowned woman holds a torch or flaming object in one hand and an ornate vessel in the other. A banner associated with the image appears to bear 'FAMA' text, linking this card to the personification of Fame or Renown. Unlike the standard two-vessel pouring of Temperance, this Viéville figure is more heraldic, her attributes transformed into emblems of proclamation.

trump-15.name: XV · Le Diable
trump-15.Scene: A large hairy bestial creature with green-tinged fur and broad bat wings fills the upper portion of the card, its arms clutching smaller human figures. There is no pedestal and no chained couple — the Viéville Devil is wilder and more feral than many Marseille counterparts, a creature of abduction rather than bondage.

trump-16.name: XVI · La Maison-Dieu
trump-16.Scene: A large leafy tree stands at center, struck from above by a radiant disc or sun-burst. Small coins or drops fall from the branches, and two small human figures stand at the base looking up. The Viéville does not depict a tower struck by lightning — a tree is the locus of the celestial blow, one of the deck's most distinctive iconographic substitutions.

trump-17.name: XVII · L'Étoile
trump-17.Scene: A bearded scholarly man sits before a building or architectural backdrop, holding a plant branch extended toward a large central star. Small drops fall around him. The Viéville L'Étoile replaces the conventional nude woman pouring water at a riverbank with a male figure in a semi-interior setting — the star is studied, not bathed under.

trump-18.name: XVIII · La Lune
trump-18.Scene: A large round full-faced moon shines with radiating beams above a leafy tree. Below it, a woman sits and spins using a distaff, her domestic labor placed under the moon's watch. There are no dogs, no crayfish, no towers — the Viéville Moon is a domestic night scene, the lunation presiding over textile work and the rhythms of household time.

trump-19.name: XVIIII · Le Soleil
trump-19.Scene: A radiant human-faced sun shines from the upper portion of the card, its face expressive and personified. Below, a semi-nude young figure rides a horse sidesaddle, holding a red banner or flag. The Viéville Soleil is unusually dynamic — the rider on horseback with a banner suggests solar procession and triumph rather than the playful children of other traditions.

trump-20.name: XX · Le Jugement
trump-20.Scene: A chubby putto sits in the clouds playing a lute, its small wings spread. Below, two bearded men kneel on the ground, looking upward toward the musical angel. The Viéville Jugement replaces the traditional trumpet-blowing angel with a lute-playing cherub — music rather than apocalypse, intimate rather than eschatological.

trump-21.name: XXI · Le Monde
trump-21.Scene: A haloed central figure stands within a wreath of laurel, arms slightly spread. In the upper corners, two winged angels hover. In the lower corners, a lion appears at left and a bull or ox at lower right — two of the four evangelist symbols framing the mandorla of the World figure.

epees-22.name: Roi de Épées
epees-22.Scene: An armored king sits on a low decorated pedestal, wearing a large wide-brimmed hat with a golden crown topping it. His dark purple cape falls over blue-gray plate armor with red accents and gold decorative buckles at the waist. A long sword extends diagonally to his right, blade tall. Small foliage marks the base.

epees-23.name: Reine de Épées
epees-23.Scene: A crowned queen sits on a golden throne with curved armrests. Her long red gown is overlaid with a dark purple-black mantle, and her fair hair falls loose beneath the crown. She holds a long vertical sword at her right side, blade pointing upward. Her expression is composed and frontal.

epees-24.name: Cavalier de Épées
epees-24.Scene: An armored knight rides a tan horse with red decorative caparison and red bridle. He wears a golden helmet and holds a long diagonal sword over his shoulder, blade angling upward. The horse's hooves and the rider's posture convey controlled forward motion. Decorative flowers appear at the card's base.

epees-25.name: Valet de Épées
epees-25.Scene: A young standing figure wears a flat red beret with a small gold ornament and a colorful doublet in red, purple, and gold. He holds one sword by the hilt in his left hand, the blade angling diagonally across his body. His right hand rests at his belt. Ground-level foliage frames his feet.

epees-26.name: Dix de Épées
epees-26.Scene: A single large sword is gripped at its decorated hilt in the lower portion of the card, its long blade rising diagonally. Red oval and teardrop shapes are scattered around the blade, suggesting falling drops or scattered sparks. The ten of swords is reduced to one dominant blade rather than an array of ten.

epees-27.name: Neuf de Épées
epees-27.Scene: Nine sword blades are arranged in the Marseille convention, their hilts and tips distributed in a pattern of crossed and parallel arrangements. Red and gold accents at the hilts break the gray of the blades. Decorative foliage or small floral elements fill the interstices.

epees-28.name: Huit de Épées
epees-28.Scene: Eight sword blades are distributed in a symmetrical interlace pattern typical of Viéville pip cards. The hilts carry red and gold detailing, and the overall arrangement is dense and geometric. Small decorative elements appear at the card's margins.

epees-29.name: Sept de Épées
epees-29.Scene: Seven sword blades are arranged in an asymmetric but balanced formation. The central blade is typically longer or more prominent. Red and gold hilt details and small foliage elements complete the composition in the Viéville's characteristic palette.

epees-30.name: Six de Épées
epees-30.Scene: Six sword blades are distributed in two trios or a three-by-two arrangement, their hilts marked with red and gold. The design is more open than the higher pip numbers, with decorative elements given more space between the blades.

epees-31.name: Cinq de Épées
epees-31.Scene: Five sword blades are arranged with one at center and two flanking each side. The Viéville five of swords carries a slight imbalance to its composition, the central blade asserting dominance over the flanking pairs. Red and gold hilt details animate the gray blades.

epees-32.name: Quatre de Épées
epees-32.Scene: Four sword blades are arranged in a cross or square pattern, their hilts meeting toward the center. The composition is more spacious than the higher numbers, each blade given room. Red and gold accents at guard and pommel mark the Viéville style.

epees-33.name: Trois de Épées
epees-33.Scene: Three sword blades cross at or near the card's center, their hilts at three corners. The crossing of three blades creates a focal point of intersection. Small decorative elements in red and gold animate the spaces between.

epees-34.name: Deux de Épées
epees-34.Scene: Two sword blades cross in an X formation at the card's center. Red and gold hilt details mark each blade's end. Small decorative elements fill the four quadrants formed by the crossing, this being the most elemental pip image of the suit.

epees-35.name: As de Épées
epees-35.Scene: Two swords cross in a starburst arrangement at the card's center, forming a dominant diamond shape with decorative elements radiating outward and small shapes scattered at the margins. The Viéville ace of swords is bold and heraldic, the suit's essential force concentrated in its most elemental emblem.

suit-epees.name: Épées · Swords
suit-epees.Scene: The suit of Épées (Swords) in the Viéville Tarot spans fourteen ranks from Roi to As. The court figures follow standard Marseille conventions — seated king, enthroned queen, mounted knight, standing valet — while the pip cards arrange silver-gray blades in symmetrical formations characteristic of the 17th-century Parisian woodcut tradition.

deniers-36.name: Roi de Deniers
deniers-36.Scene: A large golden coin fills the center of the card, bearing an ornate cross-and-clover design within a ring of alternating red and gold triangular rays. Above and below the coin, several lines of old French verse are inscribed in bold medieval lettering, beginning 'PERE SAINCT EAIT MOYVVRTICE DE CE...' and ending with references to the Pope, Papesse, Emperor, and Sun. This is one of the most textually unusual cards in the deck.

deniers-37.name: Reine de Deniers
deniers-37.Scene: A large S-shaped scroll or ribbon curves vertically through the card, its golden body bearing the maker's inscription 'IACQUE VIEVIL A PARIS.' Two small coin circles are embedded in the upper and lower loops of the S. Decorative elements — arrows, vines, or scrollwork — appear at the sides. This is the Viéville deck's remarkable self-identification card.

deniers-38.name: Cavalier de Deniers
deniers-38.Scene: Three golden starburst coins are arranged among dense interlacing red and gold vine-and-leaf foliage. The coins' surfaces bear radiating petal or ray designs. The entire composition is lush and ornamental, the three deniers nested within elaborate botanical surround.

deniers-39.name: Valet de Deniers
deniers-39.Scene: Eight elongated cylindrical objects in red are arranged in two overlapping diamond or oval crosshatch formations, creating a dense geometric pattern. The composition is abstract and heraldic rather than figurative, unusual for a court card. The Viéville valet de deniers expresses rank through pattern rather than person.

deniers-40.name: Dix de Deniers
deniers-40.Scene: Ten golden starburst coins are arranged in a symmetrical pattern across the card. Interlacing red and gold vine elements fill the spaces between the coins, typical of the suit's ornamental pip treatment. The ten-coin card represents the suit at its fullest extension.

deniers-41.name: Neuf de Deniers
deniers-41.Scene: Nine golden starburst coins are distributed across the card in the Viéville Marseille convention, balanced across upper and lower halves. Red and gold vine elements complete the interstices. The nine-coin card is rich and dense without yet reaching the fullness of the ten.

deniers-42.name: Huit de Deniers
deniers-42.Scene: Eight golden coins are arranged in two rows of four or in a symmetrical interlocking pattern. The Viéville eight of coins has the balance and geometric elegance common to the suit's mid-range pips, the starburst coins evenly spaced among vine-and-leaf ornaments.

deniers-43.name: Sept de Deniers
deniers-43.Scene: Seven golden starburst coins are distributed in an asymmetric but visually weighted arrangement. Red and gold decorative elements animate the spaces between the coins in the Viéville ornamental tradition. The seven-coin card has a quality of active rather than settled accumulation.

deniers-44.name: Six de Deniers
deniers-44.Scene: Six golden starburst coins are arranged in two trios or a two-by-three grid, with ample space between them for the vine-and-leaf ornaments characteristic of the Viéville coins suit. The six-coin card is orderly and readable, the suit's ornamental vocabulary given room to breathe.

deniers-45.name: Cinq de Deniers
deniers-45.Scene: Five golden coins are placed with a central coin surrounded by four others, or in a cross formation. The Viéville five of coins uses the same starburst coin design as the rest of the suit, set against the characteristic red and gold ornamental interlace filling the card's field.

deniers-46.name: Quatre de Deniers
deniers-46.Scene: Four golden starburst coins are arranged in a square or two-by-two pattern. The spacious composition of the four-coin card leaves room for elaborate vine-and-leaf ornaments in the Viéville manner, giving the card a calm, architectural quality.

deniers-47.name: Trois de Deniers
deniers-47.Scene: Three golden starburst coins are placed at three corners of an implied triangle, connected by red vine stems. The Viéville three of coins has a triangular tension that the rest of the suit lacks — three coins in active relation suggesting relationship and dynamic rather than static accumulation.

deniers-48.name: Deux de Deniers
deniers-48.Scene: Two golden coins are placed at upper and lower portions of the card, flanked by ornamental vine work. The Viéville two of coins holds the suit's primal duality — two starburst discs in vertical correspondence, the simplest expression of exchange and balance.

deniers-49.name: As de Deniers
deniers-49.Scene: A single large golden coin occupies the card's center, its starburst or sunflower-ray design rendered with particular care. Ornamental elements surround it, giving this ace an emblem-like quality — both the seed of the suit and its essential visual statement.

suit-deniers.name: Deniers · Coins
suit-deniers.Scene: The suit of Deniers (Coins) in the Viéville Tarot is among the most textually and iconographically distinctive in the surviving Marseille tradition. The Roi de Deniers bears a verse inscription, the Reine carries the maker's S-scroll 'IACQUE VIEVIL A PARIS,' and the pip cards display golden starburst coins in ornate red-and-gold vine interlace throughout.

batons-50.name: Roi de Bâtons
batons-50.Scene: A standing figure in a broad-brimmed hat with gold-and-red doublet and red hose holds up a single large golden coin in his raised right hand. A second coin lies at his feet on the grassy ground. The figure is depicted frontally without a throne, his standing posture and coins distinguishing this unusual Viéville king from the typically enthroned Roi of other Marseille decks.

batons-51.name: Reine de Bâtons
batons-51.Scene: A bearded man in profile strides forward, a feathered cap on his head. Three red batons are slung diagonally across his back and chest. A small dog follows at his left heel, and a bundle or sack is visible at his back. The Viéville Reine de Bâtons is depicted as a wandering figure in motion rather than a court figure in repose.

batons-52.name: Cavalier de Bâtons
batons-52.Scene: Eight elongated blue-gray baton shafts, each marked with red oval nodes, are arranged in two overlapping diamond formations creating a complex crosshatch pattern. Gold foliage and small blue flowers occupy the spaces between the batons. The cavalier of batons is rendered as pure geometric ornament rather than figured scene.

batons-53.name: Valet de Bâtons
batons-53.Scene: Nine blue-gray or gray baton shafts with red oval nodes and gold finials radiate outward from intersecting crossing points. Red acanthus or vine bands cross the shafts at nodes, and gold leaf motifs fill the spaces. The composition approaches the density of the ten while retaining visual distinction for each shaft.

batons-54.name: Dix de Bâtons
batons-54.Scene: Ten red baton shafts are arranged in the dense interlocking pattern typical of the Viéville batons suit, their cylindrical forms overlapping and crossing. Gold and red ornamental elements fill the interstices. The ten of batons is the most crowded of the suit's pip cards, a testament to accumulated energy reaching its limit.

batons-55.name: Neuf de Bâtons
batons-55.Scene: Nine red baton shafts are distributed in a crossing arrangement with decorative foliage between them. The nine of batons approaches the density of the ten but retains slightly more breathing room, the arrangement active and near its peak. Red and gold animate the design.

batons-56.name: Huit de Bâtons
batons-56.Scene: Eight red baton shafts cross in two groups of four, creating interlocking X shapes with ornamental elements between. The geometric clarity of the eight-fold arrangement gives this card a symmetrical, organized quality. Gold and decorative details mark the nodes.

batons-57.name: Sept de Bâtons
batons-57.Scene: Seven red baton shafts are arranged in a slightly asymmetric pattern, with one typically dominant over the others. The Viéville seven of batons has the characteristic tension of odd-number cards, the visual imbalance suggesting active engagement rather than settled arrangement.

batons-58.name: Six de Bâtons
batons-58.Scene: Six red baton shafts are arranged in two groups of three or in a symmetrical pattern with open spacing. The mid-range six of batons has a quality of equilibrium, the suit's energy at a point of potential balance, the red cylinders spaced with room for decorative elements to show.

batons-59.name: Cinq de Bâtons
batons-59.Scene: Five red baton shafts are arranged with a central dominant baton and two flanking each side. The five of batons carries the suit's characteristic vitality, the five-fold arrangement suggesting encounter or contest between multiple active forces. Gold decorative elements fill the card.

batons-60.name: Quatre de Bâtons
batons-60.Scene: Four red baton shafts are arranged in a square or cross pattern, their cylindrical forms clearly spaced. The four of batons is among the more open pip cards of the suit, the arrangement stable and grounded. Gold and red decorative elements fill the generous spaces between.

batons-61.name: Trois de Bâtons
batons-61.Scene: Three red baton shafts are arranged at three points, their placement suggesting a triangle of force. The Viéville three of batons has a dynamic triangular quality, the three cylinders in active relation with ornamental elements occupying the spaces between them.

batons-62.name: Deux de Bâtons
batons-62.Scene: Two red baton shafts cross or stand in parallel relation in the card's field, flanked by ornamental elements. The two of batons is the suit's primal crossing or pairing — two forces in initial relation, the minimal expression of active energy.

batons-63.name: As de Bâtons
batons-63.Scene: A single large red baton shaft dominates the card, its cylindrical form rising from base to tip with ornamental elements framing it on either side. The Viéville ace of batons is bold and direct, the suit's fundamental energy expressed in one concentrated emblem.

suit-batons.name: Bâtons · Batons
suit-batons.Scene: The suit of Bâtons (Batons) in the Viéville Tarot is rendered in deep red for the baton shafts, with gold and blue-gray ornamental interlace throughout the pip cards. The court figures are iconographically unusual — a standing man holding coins serves as king, a striding man with dog as queen — while the pip cards arrange red cylindrical batons in dense crossing formations.

coupes-64.name: Roi de Coupes
coupes-64.Scene: An elaborate architectural chalice or grail rises from a stepped and decorated base, its rounded bowl richly ornamented with crosshatch patterns and a central motif. From the rim of the cup rise multiple turret-like or candle-like forms in alternating blue-gray and gold, giving the vessel a castle-like quality. The Viéville king of cups is one of the most elaborate objects in the suit.

coupes-65.name: Reine de Coupes
coupes-65.Scene: Three golden cups with rounded lower bodies are arranged on vine stems, the upper portions of two side cups bearing dragon or animal-head forms. Below the cups, a verse is inscribed in bold old French lettering referencing the moon, the stars, lightning, force, hanging, and the devil. The Viéville queen of cups carries a cryptic narrative text alongside its three cups.

coupes-66.name: Cavalier de Coupes
coupes-66.Scene: Three golden cups with fluted lower bowls and rounded upper forms are arranged among dense interlacing red and gold foliage. The cups' interiors show red and their exteriors are gold with detailed surface patterning. The cavalier of cups is rendered as a lush botanical arrangement of cups nested in ornamental vines.

coupes-67.name: Valet de Coupes
coupes-67.Scene: A young figure in a red-and-gold plumed cap stands facing left, holding a large tall baton or lance at his left side while his right arm is raised or gesturing. The card is labeled Valet de Coupes but depicts a figure whose visible attribute is a baton rather than a cup — one of the Viéville deck's characteristic iconographic crossings between suits.

coupes-68.name: Dix de Coupes
coupes-68.Scene: Ten golden cups are arranged across the card in the Viéville pip convention, their fluted forms distributed in a symmetric pattern. The suit's characteristic ornamental foliage fills the spaces between the cups. The ten of cups marks the suit's fullness, all cups present in a completed field.

coupes-69.name: Neuf de Coupes
coupes-69.Scene: Nine golden cups are distributed across the card, approaching the density and fullness of the ten but retaining slightly more visual breathing room. Red and gold vine ornaments fill the interstices. The nine of cups carries a quality of near-satisfaction, the suit almost complete.

coupes-70.name: Huit de Coupes
coupes-70.Scene: Eight golden cups are arranged in two groups of four or in a symmetrical pattern across the card. The Viéville eight of cups has the geometric balance characteristic of the suit's mid-range pips, the fluted cup forms evenly distributed with ornamental elements between them.

coupes-71.name: Sept de Coupes
coupes-71.Scene: Seven golden cups are distributed in an asymmetric but visually weighted arrangement. The Viéville seven of cups carries the slight imbalance of odd-number cards, the arrangement suggesting multiple emotional channels rather than a single directed flow.

coupes-72.name: Six de Coupes
coupes-72.Scene: Six golden cups are arranged in two trios or a three-by-two pattern, with ornamental elements given generous space between them. The six of cups in the Viéville is open and harmonious, the suit's characteristic warmth expressed in a balanced arrangement that invites reception.

coupes-73.name: Cinq de Coupes
coupes-73.Scene: Five golden cups are placed with a central cup prominent and two flanking each side, set against the red-and-gold ornamental interlace. The odd-number instability of the five suggests a moment of emotional imbalance or questioning within the field of abundance.

coupes-74.name: Quatre de Coupes
coupes-74.Scene: Four golden cups are arranged in a square or two-by-two formation, their fluted forms clearly spaced with ornamental elements between them. The four of cups has a quality of stable containment — the suit at a structural four-fold point, emotions held in a firm and regular arrangement.

coupes-75.name: Trois de Coupes
coupes-75.Scene: Three golden cups are arranged at three points, their forms connected by vine stems or ornamental interlace. The three of cups has a triangular vitality — three vessels in active relation, the suit's emotional energy distributed among three distinct but connected forms.

coupes-76.name: Deux de Coupes
coupes-76.Scene: Two golden cups stand at upper and lower positions in the card, flanked or connected by ornamental elements. The Viéville two of cups holds the primal emotional dyad — two vessels in simple vertical correspondence, the beginning of exchange and reciprocity.

coupes-77.name: As de Coupes
coupes-77.Scene: A single large golden cup occupies the center of the card, its form decorated with the suit's characteristic surface patterning and ornamental elements surrounding it. The Viéville ace of cups is the most concentrated expression of the suit — one vessel, fully present, awaiting what it will receive or bestow.

suit-coupes.name: Coupes · Cups
suit-coupes.Scene: The suit of Coupes (Cups) in the Viéville Tarot ranges across fourteen ranks from Roi to As. The cup forms are distinctive throughout — architectural and multi-tiered in the king's chalice, dragon-crowned in the queen's three-cup arrangement, and fluted in gold throughout the pip cards. Several cards in the suit bear old French inscriptions or verse, giving the Viéville cups their unique narrative character.

trump-mat.name: Le Mat (The Fool)
trump-mat.Scene: A walking figure in a red hat strides forward, carrying in both hands a large ornate golden cup or grail. This is an extraordinary departure from the standard Marseille Fool with stick and bundle — the Viéville Le Mat holds a magnificent chalice, associating foolishness with wealth or sacred vessel rather than vagabondage.

axis-atouts.name: Les Atouts (22 Trumps)
axis-atouts.Scene: A navigational axis grouping all twenty-two Viéville trumps together — from Le Bateleur through Le Monde, with Le Mat at the unnumbered threshold. The axis invites reading across this deck's many iconographic departures: the standing Pendu, the tree-struck Maison-Dieu, the lute-playing Jugement, the grail-carrying Fou, and the domestic Moon.
